text: Few comments: @user - I 100% agree with that and the the following two paragraphs. I think it's conceptually aligned with what I also wrote above: "when observing PodGroup marked for deletion, ensure that all pods that are not yet marked for deletion, explicitly delete them (those are the ones that are created under this race). This means we have a race with scheduler deleting those though." So I agree that it comes with certain consequences and implications on every single controller integrating with our API. I like that too for a reason that it scopes the logic to a single component. This however would come with certain API-level changes, at least (probably more): a) We need more mutability at PodGroup - we need to be able to add/remove DRA resources to existing PodGroups (e.g. to deallocate ResourceClaim) b) We need to change the semantics of conditions - the "PodGroupInitiallyScheduled" no longer really makes sense then as after preemption PodGroup should go through initial scheduling again. So in fact this condition is no longer terminal (it's rather per "incarnation") I'm also still wondering if that really means no additional requirements on integrating controllers. As long as we talk about label-based TAS, when we will have no running pods in the new incarnations, it should just work out-of-the-box. But if we start talking about DRA, let's imagine a case where I want to have a Job that shares a single ResourceClaim: - when initially created, the RC is not yet allocated and it's get scheduled and allocated on first pod scheduling - then we preempt the whole PodGroup - we expect that to effectively also deallocate this RC (to free up those resources) - so the new pods should now have effectively go through new scheduling from scratch - but we will still use the same ResourceClaim My understanding is that a given ResourceClaim can switch between allocated->deallocated->allocated states any number of times, which means that it should just work if we do that right (we may need additional synchronization with deallocation controllers though). But adding also @user to confirm ^^ I will think about it, but for now I'm closer to this model.
